coord_notes.kind: The forward map is \(\mathrm{id}_\Theta\). The update \(W_{t+1}=W_t+P_t\phi_t(\hat S_t)\) compresses the gradient by \(P_t^\top\) and anchors it by \(P_t\) (Def IV.1).
coord_notes.shape: Per step the reachable set is the moving linear space \(\{W_t+P_tX\}\). The anchor is constant within a step, so Prop IV.2 applies with period 1.
coord_notes.base_point: Each step is a linear method at its own base, hence regular.
coord_notes.covariance: \(P_t\) tracks online PCA of \(\tilde G=G/\lVert G\rVert\). The loss \(\lVert PP^\top\tilde G-\tilde G\rVert^2\) is \(O(m)\)-equivariant on the left, and it sees the right side only through \(\tilde G\tilde G^\top\). So the frame geometry is \(CO\times CO\) of the gradient, as for GaLore. An Adam-type OptimizerP on \(P\) cuts the left side down to signed permutations.
coord_notes.merge: The method writes the full weight directly.
coord_notes.rebasing: A rebasing scheme with period 1. The frame moves every step, so the reach is all of \(\Theta\). The subspace optimizer state is carried across rebasings without transport.

methods.categorical_reading: A backward lens \((\mathrm{id}_\Theta;\,c_t=P_t^\top,\,a_t=P_t)\) whose frame takes one online-PCA gradient step per iteration. By the degree-one collapse (Prop IV.2), each step is the one-sided method \(\mathrm{FB}(P_t)\) re-based at \(\theta_t\). It sits in GaLore's row of the cotangent table, with the periodic SVD replaced by a frame that moves every step.

arrows.note: Within one step at base \(\theta_t\), OSD is \(\mathrm{FB}(P_t):X\mapsto\theta_t+P_tX\), the frozen-\(B\) sub-object of LoRA pointed at \((P_t,0)\).

obstructions.reason: Over \(T\) steps OSD reaches \(\theta_k+\sum_tP_t\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), of dimension up to \(\min(m,Tr)\,n>rn\), so it does not factor through one GaLore period.

methods.check_notes: All seven coordinates re-derived and confirmed: B, moving Lin {W_t+P_tX}, regular, none, OxO (online-PCA loss is O(m)-equivariant and sees the right side only through G~G~^T, consistent with GaLore), na, schedule. A2 arrow into LoRA pointed at (P_t,0) by freezing B=P_t confirmed (as for GaLore). The O2 obstruction to one GaLore period is valid. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Forward map \(\mathrm{id}_\Theta\) and no gradient compression (\(c_t=a_t=\mathrm{id}\)). Only `opt` changes: one second-moment scalar per Hessian block. As an object it is Full FT, the terminal object.
coord_notes.shape: The anchor is the identity, so the per-step image is all of \(\Theta\): Lin, with \(d=\dim\Theta\).
coord_notes.covariance: The image is \(\Theta\), so \(GL\times GL\). The optimizer's own equivariance is smaller. \(v_b\) is a Frobenius mean over an output row (or a head), so the update is \(O(n)\)-equivariant on the input side but only signed-permutation-equivariant across output blocks. That is a symmetry of the dynamics (Exposé III), not of the image.
coord_notes.merge: The method writes the full weight directly.
coord_notes.rebasing: No schedule. The reach is already \(\Theta\) at \(K=1\), so further cycles gain nothing.

methods.categorical_reading: Adam-mini is the terminal object \(\mathrm{Full\ FT}=(\Theta,\theta_0,\mathrm{id})\) with different trained-method data: a block-scalar preconditioner replaces Adam's coordinatewise one. In the lens picture it is a backward method with trivial compression. Every difference from Adam lies in the induced cometric, not in the slice.

arrows.note: Both are the terminal object with forward map \(\mathrm{id}_\Theta\). They differ only in optimizer data (Def III.1), not as objects.

obstructions.reason: Adam-mini coarsens only the preconditioner, so its step is a full-rank matrix: \(d=\dim\Theta\), against \(rn\) for one GaLore period.

methods.check_notes: Confirmed: optimizer-only, so as an object it is Full FT. B / Lin(Theta) / regular / none / GLxGL / na / idempotent, consistent with apollo and fira in batch-6. The iso arrow to lomo (A3, h = id) and the O2 obstruction to galore (full-rank step) are valid. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Compression \(g\mapsto\langle z_t,g\rangle\) (a central difference, no reverse pass) with anchor \(\lambda\mapsto\lambda z_t\) (the table after Def IV.1).
coord_notes.shape: Each step is the linear line method \(\lambda\mapsto\theta_t+\lambda z_t\), with \(d=1\) (Thm V.3, Cor 6).
coord_notes.covariance: With \(z_t\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d)\) the method is covariant under \(O(\Theta)\) in law (Table VIII.B), but not under non-orthogonal changes of basis.
coord_notes.merge: The method writes the full weight (or a PEFT module's parameters) directly.
coord_notes.rebasing: A rebasing scheme of lines, resampled every step. Its reach is \(\Theta\), since the \(z_t\) span it.

methods.categorical_reading: MeZO is the rank-one, globally random corner of the cotangent table: a backward lens whose compression is a single directional derivative along a fresh Gaussian direction. By Prop IV.3 each step is the linear method \(\theta_t+\mathbb Rz_t\) on a moving base. So its reach is \(\Theta\), and its cometric \(\eta zz^\top\) equals \(\eta I\) only in expectation.

obstructions.reason: A MeZO step \(\lambda z_t\) has per-matrix rank \(\min(m,n)>r\), so it lies in no Flora period \(\{XA_t\}\).
For the same reason it lies in no GaLore period \(\{P_tX\}\), whose maximum rank is \(r\).

methods.check_notes: Confirmed against the periodic table and axes.json: B, moving random line, regular, none, frame (O(Theta) in law), na, schedule. O2 obstructions to flora-opt and galore are valid, because a Gaussian z reshaped per matrix has full rank almost surely. core = true is appropriate. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Plain SGD, with each tensor's update fused into the backward pass. The forward map is \(\mathrm{id}_\Theta\) and the compression is the identity. What changes is the memory schedule of the backward pass (Obs IV.4), not the parametrisation.
coord_notes.shape: The per-step image is \(\Theta\), the full gradient.
coord_notes.covariance: The image is \(\Theta\). SGD is \(O(\Theta)\)-natural, and LOMO's global-norm gradient normalisation is orthogonally invariant.
coord_notes.merge: The method writes the full weight directly.
coord_notes.rebasing: No schedule; the reach is \(\Theta\) at once.

methods.categorical_reading: LOMO is Full FT trained by SGD, with the backward lens evaluated tensor by tensor so that each parameter cotangent is consumed as soon as it is produced. It adds nothing to the object. Its contribution is an evaluation order for \(\mathsf R[f]\) that keeps only one tensor's cotangent alive.

obstructions.reason: A LOMO step uses the full gradient (\(d=\dim\Theta\)); a MeZO step moves along one random line (\(d=1\)).

methods.check_notes: Confirmed: fused SGD is Full FT with a backward evaluation order (Obs IV.4). Coordinates B / Lin / regular / none / GLxGL / na / idempotent. The O2 obstruction to mezo (per-step d = dim Theta vs 1) is valid. entry_type 'recipe' is reasonable for a memory schedule of plain SGD. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: A fused-backward update with an Adafactor-style factored second moment \(v_t=r_tc_t/(\mathbf 1^\top r_t)\) and grouped RMS normalisation. The forward map is \(\mathrm{id}_\Theta\) and the compression is the identity.
coord_notes.shape: The step \(g/\sqrt v\) is a full-rank matrix, so the image is \(\Theta\). The rank-one factorisation is of the preconditioner, not of the update.
coord_notes.covariance: The image is \(\Theta\). The factored second moment is natural only under signed row and column permutations, and the relative step \(\max(\epsilon,\mathrm{RMS}(\theta_{t-1}))\) reads the parameter tensor.
coord_notes.merge: The method writes the full weight directly.

methods.categorical_reading: AdaLomo is the terminal object with new optimizer data: a rank-one non-negative factorisation of the second moment, fused into the backward pass. Its step is scaled by \(\mathrm{RMS}(\theta)\), so the degree-one collapse excludes it (Prop IV.2). Run inside a projected or LoRA chart, it would not reproduce the full-weight trajectory.

arrows.note: The same object (Full FT). AdaLomo adds a factored adaptive learning rate, which is trained-method data.

obstructions.reason: Factoring the second moment is not compressing the gradient. AdaLomo's step has full rank, so it lies in no Flora period \(\{XA_t\}\).

methods.check_notes: Confirmed: Full FT with a factored second moment and an RMS(theta)-scaled step. Prop IV.2 excludes parameter-reading optimizers, as noted. The iso arrow to lomo and the O2 obstruction to flora-opt (full-rank step) are valid. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: A post-hoc operation \(\Theta^N\to\Theta\), \((\theta_i)\mapsto\frac1{|S|}\sum_{i\in S}\theta_i\), on fine-tuned checkpoints that share \(\theta_0\).
coord_notes.shape: n/a: there are no continuous coefficients. The uniform soup is one point, and the greedy soup is a finite search over subset barycentres in \(\mathrm{aff}\{\theta_i\}\). Neither has a germ at \(\theta_0\).
coord_notes.base_point: Barycentric: the weights sum to 1, so no admissible choice returns \(\theta_0\) (generically \(\theta_0\notin\mathrm{aff}\{\theta_i\}\)). The operation never uses \(\theta_0\).
coord_notes.gauge: n/a: there are no trainable parameters, so there is no fibre to read.
coord_notes.covariance: Averaging commutes with every affine map of \(\Theta\), translations included: \(\mathrm{Aff}(\Theta)\supseteq GL(\Theta)\supseteq GL\times GL\).
coord_notes.rebasing: n/a: a one-shot post-hoc operation, so merge-and-restart does not apply (– in Table VIII.B).

methods.categorical_reading: A soup is the barycentre map of the affine space \(\Theta\), applied to a tuple of trained points. It is natural under all of \(\mathrm{Aff}(\Theta)\), and unlike task arithmetic it never refers to the base point. As an object it is the point \(\lambda=\mathbf 1_S/|S|\) of task arithmetic's coefficient family, and so it lives in the unpointed slice.

arrows.note: The soup is the point \(\lambda=\mathbf 1_S/|S|\) of task arithmetic's family. This is an arrow of the unpointed slice (task arithmetic pointed at \(h(\ast)\)).

methods.check_notes: Confirmed: P, shape/gauge/rebasing n/a (a single point or a finite subset search, no germ at theta0, no trainable coefficients), unpointed (barycentric weights never return theta0), GLxGL (affine-natural), M1. The arrow to task-arithmetic at lambda = 1_S/|S| satisfies rho_TA(h(*)) = soup, in the unpointed slice. core = true is reasonable for a landmark merging method. No changes. coord_notes.kind: Post hoc, \(\Theta^N\to\Theta\): a per-coordinate precision-weighted mean of fine-tuned checkpoints.
coord_notes.shape: n/a: the family \(\lambda\mapsto\sum_i\lambda_iF_i\theta_i/\sum_i\lambda_iF_i\) is rational, neither affine nor multihomogeneous, and its weights are hyperparameters.
coord_notes.base_point: Barycentric per coordinate: each merged coordinate lies between the fine-tuned ones, so \(\theta_0\) is not reached generically.
coord_notes.gauge: n/a: no trainable coefficients.
coord_notes.covariance: A diagonal Fisher transforms as \(D^{-2}F\) under a diagonal reparametrisation. So the merge is equivariant under the monomial group \(\mathrm{Mon}_N\) of \(\Theta\) (hence \(\mathrm{Mon}\times\mathrm{Mon}\) per matrix), but not under rotations. Full-Fisher merging would be \(GL(\Theta)\)-natural.

methods.categorical_reading: Fisher merging is the barycentre of the \(\theta_i\) for the diagonal metrics \(F_i\), i.e. the maximiser of a product of diagonal Laplace posteriors. The diagonal approximation fixes a privileged basis, so this is a coordinate (Mon) operation. It sits between plain soups (\(F_i=I\), affine-natural) and full-Fisher merging (\(GL\)-natural).

obstructions.reason: \(\theta^\star-\theta_0=\sum_i\mathrm{diag}\big(\lambda_iF_i/\textstyle\sum_j\lambda_jF_j\big)\tau_i\) has coordinate-dependent weights, so it lies outside \(\theta_0+\mathrm{span}\{\tau_i\}\) generically.

methods.check_notes: Confirmed: P, n/a shape/gauge/rebasing, unpointed, MonxMon, M1. numpy: equivariance under signed-diagonal-times-permutation reparametrisation (with F -> D^-2 F) holds to 2e-16. The O1 obstruction (coordinate-dependent weights leave theta0 + span tau_i) is valid. No changes. coord_notes.kind: Post hoc and closed form, per linear layer: \(W^\star=(\sum_iW_i\tilde G_i)(\sum_i\tilde G_i)^{-1}\).
coord_notes.shape: n/a: there is no coefficient family. The shrinkage \(\alpha\) is a fixed hyperparameter and enters rationally.
coord_notes.base_point: A matrix-weighted barycentre, with weights summing to \(I\). It does not reach \(W_0\), and the formula never uses \(W_0\).
coord_notes.gauge: n/a: no trainable coefficients.
coord_notes.covariance: Under \(W\mapsto gWh^{-1}\) with \(G_i\mapsto hG_ih^\top\), \(W^\star\mapsto gW^\star h^{-1}\) for all \(g,h\) when \(\alpha=1\) (\(GL\times GL\)). The diagonal shrinkage \(\alpha<1\) commutes only with monomial \(h\), so the default is \(GL\times\mathrm{Mon}\): the MonxGL key, with the monomial side on the input.

methods.categorical_reading: RegMean is a barycentre of the linear maps \(W_i\), weighted by their input Gram matrices: the least-squares map that reproduces every model on its own inputs. It does not use \(\theta_0\), and at \(\alpha=1\) it is \(GL\times GL\)-natural. The off-diagonal shrinkage is what brings back a privileged input basis.

obstructions.reason: \(W^\star-W_0=\sum_i\Delta W_i\tilde G_i(\sum_j\tilde G_j)^{-1}\) right-multiplies each update by a matrix weight, so it leaves \(W_0+\mathrm{span}\{\Delta W_i\}\) generically.

methods.check_notes: Confirmed: P, n/a, unpointed, MonxGL (output GL, input monomial), M1. numpy: equivariance error at alpha = 1 is 1e-15 for GL inputs, so GLxGL. At alpha = 0.9 it is 0.24 for GL inputs and 4e-16 for monomial inputs. The O1 obstruction to task arithmetic (matrix weights G~_i (sum G~)^{-1}) is valid. No changes. coord_notes.kind: A post-hoc operation on task vectors \(\tau_i=\theta_i-\theta_0\).
coord_notes.shape: Read on the coefficient family \(\lambda\mapsto\theta_0+\sum_i\lambda_i\tau_i\), which is the Table VIII.B cell. It is affine, with \(d=\dim\mathrm{span}\{\tau_i\}\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(\lambda=0\) returns \(\theta_0\), and the map is injective for independent \(\tau_i\), so the point is regular. Table VIII.B leaves this cell blank.
coord_notes.gauge: The family is injective for linearly independent task vectors.
coord_notes.covariance: \(GL(\Theta)\)-equivariant on updates (Prop V.4(c)), a group that contains \(GL\times GL\).
coord_notes.rebasing: A fixed linear shape with frozen task vectors, so idempotent (Thm V.3, Cor 2). Table VIII.B leaves this cell blank.

methods.categorical_reading: Task arithmetic uses the vector-space structure of \(T_{\theta_0}\Theta\) post hoc: its coefficient family is the linear method spanned by the task vectors, pointed at \(\lambda=0\). It is the \(GL(\Theta)\)-natural merge. For LoRA inputs it is the gauge-invariant rule, landing in \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{Nr}\) (Prop V.4(a)).

arrows.note: Global coefficients are the layer-constant points of AdaMerging's family (AdaMerging pointed at \(h(0)=0\), not at its \(0.3\) init).
For LoRA task vectors \(\tau_i=B_iA_i\), task arithmetic is the layer-constant sub-object of CAT.
With two LoRA updates, scalar weights are constant merger vectors (ZipLoRA pointed at \(m=0\), not at its all-ones init).

obstructions.reason: Take generic modules, whose \(N^2\) products \(B_iA_j\) are linearly independent. Then LoraHub's \(\sum_{i,j}w_iw_jB_iA_j\) equals \(\sum_i\lambda_iB_iA_i\) only if \(w_iw_j=0\) for \(i\ne j\), so only one module can be active. O2 also applies: LoraHub's updates have rank \(\le r\), against up to \(\min(Nr,m,n)\) for task arithmetic.

methods.check_notes: Coordinates (P, Lin, regular, none, GLxGL, M1, idempotent), read on the coefficient family, re-derived and confirmed. GL(Theta)-naturality is from Prop V.4(c). Arrows confirmed: to adamerging (layer-constant points), to lora-soups (layer-constant CAT points) and to ziplora (constant merger vectors). The targets are re-pointed at 0 where their init is a defect. Obstruction to lorahub: genericity condition added (the B_iA_j must be linearly independent; numpy check: rank 16 = N^2), and the extra O2 rank bound recorded.

coord_notes.kind: A post-hoc operation on task vectors: trim, elect sign, disjoint mean.
coord_notes.shape: Read on the scale: \(\lambda\mapsto\theta_0+\lambda\tau_m\) is a line. The trim–elect–mean map that produces \(\tau_m\) is non-linear in its inputs; the covariance axis records that.
coord_notes.base_point: \(\lambda=0\) returns \(\theta_0\), and the line is injective.
coord_notes.gauge: The line is injective (\(\tau_m\ne0\)).
coord_notes.covariance: With sign election by total mass, equivariant under \(\mathbb R^\times\cdot B_N\), homotheties times signed coordinate permutations (Prop V.4(c)). It fails under generic positive diagonals, so only the signed-permutation part of \(\mathrm{Mon}\times\mathrm{Mon}\) survives.
coord_notes.rebasing: Idempotent with \(\tau_m\) frozen. Recomputing the task vectors at the new base changes the line.

methods.categorical_reading: TIES applies a coordinatewise, magnitude- and sign-dependent operation to task vectors in \(T_{\theta_0}\Theta\), followed by the line method \(\theta_0+\mathbb R\tau_m\). Its naturality group is \(\mathbb R^\times\cdot B_N\): it presupposes the coordinate basis and is not \(O(N)\)-natural. Applied to LoRA factors (HF's non-SVD `ties`), it is also gauge-dependent.

obstructions.reason: Trimming and disjoint means act coordinatewise, so \(\tau_m\) is generically not in \(\mathrm{span}\{\tau_i\}\).

methods.check_notes: Confirmed: P, Lin read on the lambda-line theta0 + lambda tau_m, regular, none, MonxMon (only R^x . B_N survives, per Prop V.4(c)), M1, idempotent with tau_m frozen. The O1 obstruction to task arithmetic is valid generically. No changes. Sync with the refereed paper (2026-10-03): the equivariance is stated for sign election by total mass (HF's "frequency" option breaks sign flips).

coord_notes.kind: A post-hoc pre-processing operator on task vectors, applied before a merge rule.
coord_notes.shape: Read on the scale of the merge it feeds: \(\lambda\mapsto\theta_0+\lambda\sum_i\hat\tau_i\) (DARE+TA), a random line.
coord_notes.base_point: \(\lambda=0\) returns \(\theta_0\).
coord_notes.gauge: The line is injective.
coord_notes.covariance: \(D(m\odot\tau)=m\odot D\tau\) for every invertible diagonal \(D\), so the torus acts exactly, signs included. i.i.d. masks are permutation-invariant in law, so the group contains \(\mathrm{Mon}_N\) (Prop V.4(c)). It is not \(O(N)\).
coord_notes.rebasing: Idempotent with the mask frozen. Fresh masks in each cycle move the line.

methods.categorical_reading: DARE is a random coordinate mask with inverted-dropout rescaling: a pre-processing operator on \(T_{\theta_0}\Theta\) that is exactly natural under the torus and natural under permutations in law. It preserves each task vector in expectation, so DARE+TA equals task arithmetic in law, not mask by mask.

obstructions.reason: For a fixed mask, \(\sum_im_i\odot\tau_i/(1-p)\) leaves \(\mathrm{span}\{\tau_i\}\) generically. It agrees with task arithmetic only in expectation.

methods.check_notes: Confirmed: P, Lin (random line), regular, none, MonxMon (torus exactly, permutations in law; within GL x GL the monomial group is exactly Mon x Mon), M1, idempotent with the mask frozen. The O1 obstruction to task arithmetic for a fixed mask is valid. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Post hoc: layer-wise merge coefficients over frozen task vectors, fitted by test-time entropy minimisation.
coord_notes.shape: The coefficient family \(\lambda\mapsto\theta_0+\sum_{i,l}\lambda_i^l\tau_i^l\) is linear, with \(d=NL\) for independent layer task vectors.
coord_notes.base_point: The coefficients start at \(\lambda=0.3\), the task-arithmetic merge, rather than at \(0\). That is a pointing defect by design, \(e=0.3\sum_i\tau_i\).
coord_notes.gauge: The family is injective for independent layer task vectors.
coord_notes.covariance: A linear combination of task vectors, fitted through the function \(f_\theta\) (prediction entropy), hence \(GL\times GL\) per layer.
coord_notes.rebasing: A fixed linear shape with frozen task vectors, so idempotent.

methods.categorical_reading: AdaMerging trains a \(\oplus\) of \(NL\) frozen line methods \(\lambda\mapsto\lambda\tau_i^l\) by test-time entropy minimisation. For LoRA task vectors this is exactly CAT's coefficient object. The two differ only in loss and starting point.

arrows.note: When \(\tau_i^l=B_i^lA_i^l\), layer-wise AdaMerging and CAT are the same object (CAT pointed at \(h(q_0)\)). They differ in loss and initialisation.

obstructions.reason: \(d=NL\) layer-wise coefficients, against \(N\) global ones.

methods.check_notes: Confirmed: P, Lin (d = NL), defect by design (init lambda = 0.3 per catalog), none, GLxGL, M1, idempotent. The iso arrow to lora-soups for LoRA task vectors re-points CAT at h(q0). The O2 obstruction (NL > N) to task arithmetic is valid. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Post hoc: per-layer SVD truncation of each task matrix, then whitening of the stacked singular bases.
coord_notes.shape: Read on the scale \(\alpha\mapsto W_0+\alpha U_\perp\Sigma V_\perp^\top\), a line (the paper uses \(\alpha=1\)).
coord_notes.base_point: \(\alpha=0\) returns \(W_0\).
coord_notes.gauge: The line is injective. The per-task SVD sign gauge \((u_k,v_k)\mapsto(-u_k,-v_k)\) commutes with the polar factor and cancels in \(U_\perp\Sigma V_\perp^\top\), so the rule is a well-defined function of the task matrices.
coord_notes.covariance: Truncated SVDs and the polar factor \(U\mapsto P_UQ_U^\top\) are \(CO\)-equivariant on each side (Prop II.16), so \(CO\times CO\).
coord_notes.rebasing: Idempotent with the merged matrix frozen.

methods.categorical_reading: TSV-M works in the spectral frames of the task matrices. It truncates each matrix to its top singular triples and replaces the stacked bases by their polar factors, the nearest orthonormal frames. This is a \(CO\times CO\) (spectral) operation, and its output generally leaves the span of the task vectors.

obstructions.reason: Whitening mixes the tasks' singular bases, so in general \(U_\perp\Sigma V_\perp^\top\notin\mathrm{span}\{\Delta_i\}\): TSV-M is not a reweighted task arithmetic.

methods.check_notes: Confirmed: P, Lin on the alpha scale, regular, none, OxO, M1, idempotent. numpy: the sign gauge cancels exactly, the CO x CO equivariance error is 3e-14, and a GL output change fails (error 7.5). The O1 obstruction to task arithmetic is valid. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Post hoc: a joint SVD of the concatenated LoRA updates, after which an existing merge rule acts on the aligned factors.
coord_notes.shape: Read on the inner rule's scale \(\lambda\): \(W_0+\lambda\,U\Sigma V^{(m)\top}\), a line (task coefficients \(\lambda_i\) with task arithmetic inside).
coord_notes.base_point: \(\lambda=0\) returns \(W_0\).
coord_notes.gauge: The line is injective. Joint-SVD sign flips act on the \(V^{(i)}\) by signed coordinate permutations common to all tasks. TIES and DARE respect these, so for distinct singular values KnOTS-TIES is a function of the updates \(B_iA_i\).
coord_notes.covariance: The joint SVD gives exactly \(CO(m)\) on the output side. The inner TIES/DARE rule is coordinatewise in the \(V\)-coordinates, so only signed permutations survive on the input side. With task arithmetic inside, the method is \(GL\times GL\).
coord_notes.rebasing: Idempotent with the merged update frozen.

methods.categorical_reading: KnOTS is the joint gauge fixing of Prop V.4(b): a joint SVD of the concatenated updates produces a shared factor \(U\Sigma\), and coordinatewise merge rules then act on the task-specific factors. With task arithmetic as the inner rule it is exactly task arithmetic, since \(U\Sigma\sum_i\lambda_iV^{(i)\top}=\sum_i\lambda_i\Delta W^{(i)}\). Its content lies in the coordinatewise rules it makes well defined.

arrows.note: With TA as the inner rule, KnOTS and task arithmetic have the same coefficient family.

obstructions.reason: KnOTS-TIES trims and elects signs in the aligned \(V\)-coordinates, not in weight coordinates. So its \(\tau_m\) differs from dense TIES, and the two lines differ.

methods.check_notes: Confirmed: P, Lin on the inner rule's scale, regular, none, M1, idempotent. Covariance: the true group with TIES/DARE inside is CO(m) x (R^x . signed perms)(n). OxO is the closest key, and the note already states this. The arrow to task-arithmetic (TA inside: U Sigma sum lambda_i V_i^T = sum lambda_i dW_i) and the O1 obstruction to dense TIES are valid. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Training-free composition of trained LoRA or (IA)\(^3\) modules in parameter space.
coord_notes.shape: n/a. For LoRA, addition \(\lambda\mapsto(\lambda B_1+(1-\lambda)B_2)(\lambda A_1+(1-\lambda)A_2)\) is a quadratic curve through \(\theta_1\) and \(\theta_2\), with no germ at \(\theta_0\). For (IA)\(^3\) it is the line through \(\theta_1\) and \(\theta_2\).
coord_notes.base_point: The barycentric addition \(\lambda\theta^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)\theta^{(2)}\) does not pass through \(\theta_0\) generically.
coord_notes.gauge: n/a: no trained coefficients. Factor-wise addition is not \(\prod GL_r\)-invariant (Prop V.4(a)), like HF's `linear`. The negation \((A,B)\mapsto(A,-B)\) equals negating \(BA\), so it is gauge-invariant.

methods.categorical_reading: CAT is a \(\oplus\)-word in the pointed slice: \(N\) frozen line methods per layer, whose sum is a linear sub-object of \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{\sum r_i}\). It combines products rather than factors, so it is gauge-invariant. That is exactly what separates it from LoraHub.

arrows.note: Per layer, into LoRA\(_{\sum r_i}\) pointed at \((0,[A_1;\dots;A_N])\). The pointing is standard iff the stacked \(A\) has full row rank (Obs I.7).
The same object as layer-wise AdaMerging on LoRA task vectors (AdaMerging pointed at \(h(q_0)\)).

coord_notes.kind: Post hoc and training-free: k-means over the rank-one units \(s_{ij}=[a_{ij},b_{ij}]\) of trained LoRAs.
coord_notes.shape: n/a: there are no coefficients (\(k\) is discrete). The output is one point of \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le k}\).
coord_notes.base_point: No parameter value returns \(\theta_0\).
coord_notes.gauge: n/a: no trained coefficients. The clustering respects only permutations of rank-one units within each module. Sign flips \((b_j,a_j)\mapsto(-b_j,-a_j)\), unit rescalings and general \(GL_r\) all change \(s_{ij}\), so the result is not a function of the adapters (Prop V.4(a)).
coord_notes.covariance: Euclidean k-means and the norm rescaling in \([a,b]\)-space are equivariant under \(O(m)\times O(n)\). They are also equivariant under a common scaling \(s\mapsto cs\), i.e. \((B,A)\mapsto(cB,cA)\), which induces the homothety \(\Delta W\mapsto c^2\Delta W\). Independent output and input scalings rescale the \(b\)- and \(a\)-blocks unequally and change the clusters. So for fixed representatives the group is \((O\times O)\cdot\mathbb R_{>0}\): the OxO key, slightly smaller than \(CO\times CO\).

methods.categorical_reading: LoRA-LEGO regroups rank-one units across modules, using the permutation part of LoRA's \(GL_r\) gauge together with the concatenation isomorphism \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\oplus\mathrm{LoRA}_s\cong\mathrm{LoRA}_{r+s}\). It fixes only the finite permutation gauge, not \(GL_r\), so it is a rule on factor representatives, not on adapters.

arrows.note: Only at \(k=\sum_ir_i=Nr\), where clusters are singletons: the output \(N^{-1/2}\sum_iB_iA_i\) is a point of CAT's family (CAT pointed at \(h(\ast)\)).

obstructions.reason: For \(k<\sum r_i\) the centroids mix units from different LoRAs, so \(\Delta W\notin\mathrm{span}\{B_iA_i\}\) generically.

coord_notes.rebasing: A fixed linear shape with frozen updates, so idempotent.

methods.categorical_reading: ZipLoRA is a \(\oplus\) of two input-scaling methods on frozen updates, i.e. a column-wise (IA)\(^3\) on each \(\Delta W\), pointed at the direct merge. Its image lies in the frozen-\(B\) LoRA \(\{[B_c\ B_s]Y\}\). Its overlap penalty is a loss, not part of \(\rho\).

coord_notes.shape: n/a: the fused weight is the unique least-squares minimiser, so there is no coefficient family.
coord_notes.base_point: An activation-weighted barycentre, which does not reach \(W_0\).
coord_notes.gauge: n/a: there are no coefficients; gradient fusion optimises the weight itself.
coord_notes.covariance: This is RegMean at \(\alpha=1\): exactly \(GL\times GL\)-equivariant, with the self-generated activations transforming with the input basis.

methods.categorical_reading: Mix-of-Show's gradient fusion is the RegMean barycentre at \(\alpha=1\), with Gram matrices taken from the activations each concept LoRA generates for itself. It is a basis-free merge that does not use \(\theta_0\). Its update \(\sum_i\Delta W_iG_i(\sum_jG_j)^{-1}\) is dense but still has rank \(\le\sum_ir_i\), and it leaves \(\mathrm{span}\{\Delta W_i\}\).

Mix-of-Show's fused weight is its point \(\alpha=1\), given the same Gram matrices (Mix-of-Show obtains them by sampling). This is an arrow of the unpointed slice. It is not A2, because \(\alpha=1\) is not RegMean's default \(0.9\).

methods.categorical_reading: Orthogonal adaptation is LoRA-FA whose frames are drawn from one shared orthogonal basis. Independently trained concepts are therefore sub-objects \(\mathrm{FA}(A_i)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{FA}(A_S)\) of a single linear method with stacked frozen frame \(A_S\). Merging is addition inside that linear space, which is the shared-frozen-factor fix of Prop V.4(b), and the crosstalk is \(\Delta W_jA_i^\top A_i\approx0\).

arrows.note: It is LoRA-FA\((A_i)\), with \(A_i\) an orthonormal slice of a shared random basis.
The frozen-\(A\) sub-object of LoRA pointed at \((0,A_i)\).

coord_notes.base_point: Some LoRA is always active with fixed weights, so \(\theta_0\) is never reproduced.
coord_notes.gauge: n/a: no trainable coefficients.

methods.categorical_reading: LoRA Switch is a family over the base \(T\) of denoising steps, each fibre a frozen line method. LoRA Composite is an ensemble in score space: a post-hoc operation that lands in functions rather than in \(\Theta\). Neither ever forms a single weight, which is how both avoid weight-space interference.

coord_notes.kind: A family over tasks: the task-indexed point \((A^\tau,B^\tau)=(\sum_j\alpha_{\tau j}A_j,\sum_j\alpha_{\tau j}B_j)\) of LoRA.
coord_notes.shape: For each task the inventory is free, so the fibre's image is \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\).
coord_notes.base_point: HF zero-initialises the \(B_j\), so each task fibre sits at LoRA's apex, and the routing logits have no first-order effect (Lemma II.4).
coord_notes.gauge: Joint training through the product of sums keeps the diagonal \(GL_r\), \((B_jg^{-1},gA_j)\) for all \(j\) at once (Prop V.4(a)). The allocations are trained too, which adds two symmetries. One is skill mixing: \((A_j,B_j)\mapsto(\sum_lN_{jl}A_l,\sum_lN_{jl}B_l)\) and \(\alpha_\tau\mapsto N^{-\top}\alpha_\tau\), for \(N\in GL_S\) with \(N\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\). The other is a per-task rescaling of \(\sigma(Z_\tau)\), which the normalisation removes. For \(T>S\) the generic fibre has dimension \(r^2+S(S-1)+T\) (Jacobian rank, checked numerically). All three act consistently on products, so the cross terms stay well defined. The key remains GL, on the rank and skill wires.
coord_notes.covariance: Each fibre is LoRA-type, and the joint image is covariant under simultaneous \(GL\times GL\).
coord_notes.merge: For a known task the mixed LoRA fuses. Mixed-task batches need routing, and HF implements no merge.

methods.categorical_reading: Poly is a \(T\)-point of LoRA over the base of tasks, with a shared skill inventory: \(\rho\circ a:T\to\Theta\). Its product-of-sums rule has the same form as LoraHub's, but it is trained jointly. With generic allocations fixed and fewer skills than tasks, the only symmetry on the inventory is the diagonal \(GL_r\) (checked numerically). Training the allocations adds a skill-mixing group and a normalisation scale. Either way, the cross terms are a design choice rather than an ill-definedness.

arrows.note: Copy the routing logits to every head (MHR pointed at \(h(q_0)\); its heads are initialised independently).
Fibrewise over tasks, into LoRA\(_r\) pointed at \((0,\sum_j\alpha_{\tau j}A_j^0)\).

obstructions.reason: The mixing form is the same, but each task fibre of Poly reaches all of \(\mathcal M_{\le r}\) (\(d=r(m+n-r)\)), while LoraHub's frozen modules give an \(N\)-dimensional cone.

methods.check_notes: Coordinates (F_T, Cone, apex, GL, GLxGL, M1, span) and both arrows (to mhr by copying logits, to lora fibrewise at (0, sum alpha A_j^0)) re-derived and confirmed. coord_notes.kind: A family over tasks with block-wise routing: each of \(h\) blocks of the factors has its own Poly routing.
coord_notes.shape: For each task the routed factors are free, so the fibre's image is \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\).
coord_notes.base_point: As in Poly: zero \(B_j\) and near-uniform logits, so each task fibre is at the apex.
coord_notes.gauge: Block \((k,k')\) of \(B^\tau A^\tau\) is \(B^\tau[k]A^\tau[k']\), so the rank-wire gauge is a single \(g\in GL_r\) common to all skills and blocks. Each head also carries Poly's skill-mixing group \(\{N_k\in GL_S:N_k\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\}\) and a per-(task, head) normalisation scale. For \(T>S\) the generic fibre has dimension \(r^2+hS(S-1)+Th\) (Jacobian rank, checked numerically).
coord_notes.covariance: The \(h\) blocks split \(d_{in}\) and \(d_{out}\) with separate routings, an imposed block partition. The family is covariant only under the block normaliser (\(\Pi\)).
coord_notes.merge: Merge for a known task, as in Poly.

methods.categorical_reading: MHR is Poly with its routing refined over a partition of the input and output coordinates into \(h\) blocks. It is still a \(T\)-point of LoRA, but the family now carries an imposed block structure \(\Pi\) that Poly lacks. Poly is the diagonal sub-object \(Z\mapsto Z\otimes\mathbf 1_h\).

arrows.note: Fibrewise over tasks, with \(A^\tau=\mathrm{concat}_k\sum_j\alpha_{\tau jk}A_j[k]\) and likewise \(B^\tau\). The target is LoRA pointed at \((0,A^\tau_0)\).

obstructions.reason: At equal inventory, \(d(\mathrm{MHR})-d(\mathrm{Poly})=(h-1)(S-1)(T-S)\) generically (Jacobian rank). The extra \(TS(h-1)\) logits are partly absorbed by the per-head skill-mixing and normalisation gauges. So \(d(\mathrm{MHR})>d(\mathrm{Poly})\) exactly when \(h\ge2\), \(S\ge2\) and \(T>S\), which is the multi-task regime. For \(T\le S\) the two dimensions coincide in the cases checked, and O2 does not separate them.

At T<=S the gap is 0.

coord_notes.kind: A family over inputs: the router \(R(v)=\mathrm{softmax}(W_rv)\) selects, per example, a point \(\sum_iR(v)_i\theta_i\) of an adapter's parameter space.
coord_notes.shape: Adapter experts on an extension, so the method is function-level.
coord_notes.base_point: The experts are initialised randomly and differently to break symmetry, so the merged expert is not the neutral adapter: a pointing defect.
coord_notes.gauge: Averaging forces a common gauge on all experts: one hidden-unit permutation and, under ReLU, one positive rescaling for all of them. The softmax translation \(W_r\mapsto W_r+\mathbf 1c^\top\) is a further symmetry.
coord_notes.covariance: n/a: a function-level extension (– in Table VIII.B).
coord_notes.merge: The merged expert depends on each input and is a non-linear adapter.

methods.categorical_reading: SMEAR is an \(X\)-point of an adapter extension. For each example it evaluates the adapter at the router-weighted barycentre of the expert parameters, i.e. a soup indexed by inputs. Parameter averaging is what makes the router differentiable, and it also ties all experts to one gauge representative.

coord_notes.kind: A family over tokens: at each site \(\ell(x)=\sum_is_i(x)\ell_i\) is an \(X\)-point of (IA)\(^3\).
coord_notes.shape: The scaling depends on the input, so there is no single weight-space image.
coord_notes.base_point: The experts start at \(\mathbf 1\), so every fibre is the identity scaling. The router is then inert to first order, since \(\sum_i\partial s_i\cdot\mathbf 1=\partial(\sum_is_i)=0\) (a variant of Lemma II.4).
coord_notes.gauge: The expert vectors carry no gauge. The only continuous fibre is the softmax translation \(W_g\mapsto W_g+\mathbf 1c^\top\). It is the kernel of the linear logit map rather than a group acting on the experts, so it is recorded as none (\(+d_{\rm model}\)), like FourierFT's conjugate pairs.

coord_notes.merge: The scaling depends on each token through the router.

methods.categorical_reading: MoV is an \(X\)-point of (IA)\(^3\): a router-weighted barycentre of scaling vectors, evaluated per token. At its identity initialisation the router gets no task-loss gradient until the experts separate. That is a first-order fact about the family (the zero-gate lemma), not about any single expert.

coord_notes.kind: A family over tasks: \(\omega_\tau=\mathrm{softmax}(W_Te_\tau)\) reweights \(N\) experts of rank \(r/N\), giving a task-indexed point of LoRA\(_r\).
coord_notes.shape: Per task the update is \(\sum_i\omega_{\tau i}B_iA_i=[\omega_{\tau1}B_1\cdots][A_1;\dots]\), so the fibre's image is \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\).
coord_notes.base_point: The official code zero-initialises the up-projections, so each task fibre is at the apex and the gate is inert to first order.

coord_notes.merge: The weights depend only on the task id, so there is one merged copy per task.

methods.categorical_reading: MOELoRA is a \(T\)-point of LoRA\(_r\) over tasks. The task acts on the rank wire by a block-diagonal scaling \(\mathrm{diag}(\omega_\tau\otimes\mathbf 1_{r/N})\), a sum of products rather than Poly's product of sums. Each task fibre is an ordinary mergeable LoRA.

coord_notes.kind: A family over inputs: layer-wise gates over the outputs of \(N\) frozen trained LoRAs.
coord_notes.shape: Input-dependent mixture of block outputs: function-level.
coord_notes.base_point: The softmax gates sum to 1 over frozen, nonzero experts, so no gate value reproduces \(F_\theta\). The method is unpointed: positive softmax mass always moves the output.
coord_notes.gauge: Only the gate \((e,\tau)\) is trained. \((e,\tau)\mapsto(ce,c\tau)\) leaves \(G=\mathrm{softmax}(\varepsilon/\tau)\) unchanged: a scalar slide, with charge \(\lVert e\rVert^2/\eta_e+\tau^2/\eta_\tau\) under gradient flow (the slide scales \(e\) and \(\tau\) the same way, so the loss is degree-0 homogeneous and the weighted norm is conserved). The softmax translation is a further symmetry. Table VIII.B's per-expert \(GL_r\) does not apply, because the LoRAs are frozen.
coord_notes.covariance: n/a: function-level (– in Table VIII.B).
coord_notes.merge: The gates are computed from the experts' outputs for each input.

methods.categorical_reading: MoLE is an unpointed mixture over frozen LoRAs, indexed by inputs. Its gate reads the experts' own outputs, so even with a constant gate it is a convex combination of block outputs, not a weight-space sum. It differs from X-LoRA in mixing whole-block outputs, and from LoraHub in depending on the input.

obstructions.reason: MoLE's input-dependent gates mix whole block outputs. So the realised functions are generically not \(\Phi_f\) of any single weight (M∞; whole-network non-realisability is generic, not proved), and they are not in LoraHub's weight-space image.

coord_notes.kind: A family over tokens: top-2 routing over FFN experts that share the frozen FFN and differ by LoRA deltas, plus plain LoRAs on attention.
coord_notes.shape: Each expert is a whole (gated) FFN with LoRA on its projections, so the routed mixture combines non-linear expert outputs and is function-level even per token. (The catalog's \(E_k(h)=Wh+B_kA_kh\) linearises the expert.)
coord_notes.base_point: lora_B is zero-initialised (official code), so each expert equals the frozen FFN. The kept top-2 weights are renormalised to sum to 1 (Mixtral-style, as the official code is recalled to do; not re-checked here), so the block is unchanged. Without renormalisation the block would be scaled by the kept softmax mass, which would be a defect.
coord_notes.gauge: The experts are trainable: per-expert \(GL_r\) on each adapted projection, plus the router's softmax translation.
coord_notes.covariance: n/a: function-level.
coord_notes.merge: Each token is routed to its own top-2 experts.

methods.categorical_reading: MixLoRA upcycles a dense FFN into a sparse family over tokens, whose fibres are FFN experts sharing one frozen weight. Together with the attention LoRAs it is a \(\oplus\) of an \(X\)-family with ordinary LoRA. Top-2 routing makes the gate vanish exactly on \(N-2\) experts, which separates it from dense LoRA mixtures.

obstructions.reason: The block output jumps when the second- and third-ranked experts swap: the weights agree at the tie, but the selected expert changes. So for generic trained experts MixLoRA's functions are discontinuous in the input. LoRAMoE mixes inside each linear layer with an everywhere-positive softmax, so its functions are continuous. Hence MixLoRA's routed functions are not in LoRAMoE's image.

coord_notes.kind: A family over tokens and layers: a head reads hidden states from a first pass and outputs scalings \(\lambda\in\Delta^{n-1}\) for frozen LoRAs.
coord_notes.shape: Token- and layer-dependent scalings: function-level (Table VIII.B).
coord_notes.base_point: With the softmax (HF default), the scalings sum to 1 over frozen nonzero adapters, so no head parameter reproduces \(W_0\). The method is unpointed, as prompt tuning is through positive softmax mass.

methods.categorical_reading: X-LoRA is an \(X\)-point of the CAT family: per token and layer its weight is \(W_0+\sum_i\lambda_i(x)\frac{\alpha_i}{r_i}B_iA_i\), with \(\lambda(x)\) on the simplex. The simplex constraint makes it unpointed. Because of the dual pass, the family is indexed by the base model's hidden states, not by the layer input.
